text:
Maya: Heads-up: copper-embed-v0.9 brought up on semantic-holdout. Float baseline vs int6 calibrated vs int6 per-channel. Seeing a puzzling drop in recall@10 for mid-frequency queries (freq 5-50). Sharing quick numbers.

Owen: can you paste the deltas? how big?

Maya: float r@10=0.838, int6(calib)=0.801 (delta -0.037), int6(per-channel)=0.825 (delta -0.013). recall@1 float=0.554, int6(calib)=0.506, int6(pc)=0.537. UMAP 2D scatter shows tighter clusters in float, int6(calib) has a blob in the lower-left that's mangling several topics.

Ravi: interesting that per-channel helps that much. Did you use symmetric or asymmetric quant? clipping?

Maya: int6(calib) used symmetric per-tensor with max-based range estimation. int6(per-channel) used per-channel scales with 0.5% AD clipping and bias correction.

Nina: have we tried quant-aware centroids for kmeans? centroid drift can cause cluster purity loss and affect recall for mid-frequency queries.

Maya: ran kmeans k=500 purity float=0.71, int6(calib)=0.63, int6(pc)=0.69. centroid cosine shift median float->int6(calib)=0.048, float->int6(pc)=0.021. So per-channel reduces centroid drift notably.

Owen: what's the breakdown by query length/embedding norm? could be short queries more sensitive.

Maya: split by token length: short (<=6 tokens) r@10 delta -0.02, mid (7-20) -0.06, long (>20) -0.01. Midrange gets hit worst. Also embedding L2 norm distribution shifts: int6(calib) compresses high-norm tail.

Ravi: maybe calibration took a few extreme activations and compressed the mid-range. Can you share activation histograms for the attention outputs?

Maya: uploaded per-layer activation histos to the run: https://internal.rw/runs/copper-int6-20260401. Layer 18 had a heavy outlier in float that calibration scaled to a range that squashed many mid-range values.

Nina: can we use layerwise adaptive clipping: auto-clip at p99.5 instead of max?

Maya: quick ablation: int6 + layerwise p99.5 clipping => r@10=0.819, r@1=0.529, centroid shift 0.029. Performance wise latency +4% vs per-tensor int6, memory similar.

Owen: that's a useful middle ground. How about hybrid mixed precision for a small set of layers? keep early layers int6, middle layers fp16?

Maya: tried fp16 on layers 12-20 + int6 elsewhere => r@10=0.832, r@1=0.547, latency +2% vs int6 baseline but +9% vs float. This yields near-per-channel quality without full per-channel overhead.

EvalBot: automated eval summary: dataset=semantic-holdout-v3, metrics=[recall@1,recall@10,kmeans_purity,centroid_cosine_shift], float={r1:0.554,r10:0.838,purity:0.71,centroid_shift:0.0}, int6_tensor_max={r1:0.506,r10:0.801,purity:0.63,centroid_shift:0.048}, int6_pc_clip={r1:0.537,r10:0.825,purity:0.69,centroid_shift:0.021}, int6_layer_p995={r1:0.529,r10:0.819,purity:0.68,centroid_shift:0.029}, hybrid_fp16_mid={r1:0.547,r10:0.832,purity:0.70,centroid_shift:0.015}, notes="mid-frequency queries most affected; recommended default=per-channel+0.5% clip; hybrid fp16-middle as compat profile; add midfreq smoke test".

Ravi: propose gating: overall r@10 delta <= 0.03, midfreq r@10 delta <= 0.04, centroid_shift median <=0.03. If any fail, auto-mark candidate and attach recommended profile.

Nina: add a nightly job that computes per-frequency-bin recall and posts a small CSV to /eval-exports/copper for manual checks. Also include top-50 worst midfreq queries.

Maya: will add PR with quant profiles, eval dashboards, and a small sample export. Command used:

```\nrw-eval run --model copper-embed-v0.9 --quant-profile int6_per_channel_clip0.5 --dataset semantic-holdout-v3 --metrics recall@1,recall@10,kmeans_purity,centroid_cosine_shift --out /runs/copper-int6-20260401
```

Owen: please attach the 50 worst midfreq queries to the PR for manual label review.

Maya: will do. Tagging @Ravi @Nina on the PR.

Nina: nice work. One more ask: add a small visualization (UMAP) comparing float vs quant for the sample in the PR.

Maya: done in draft PR.

Owen: thanks all. Let's keep the per-channel+clip as default unless a customer requires a smaller latency footprint; then use hybrid.

Maya: ack. Closing loop after PR merge and nightly validation :thumbsup:
